gaps.sentence: The contract, the small print of ___ nobody had read, contained a surprise clause.
gaps.explanation: After a preposition only 'which' (things) or 'whom' (people) is possible.

gaps.sentence: The assistant ___ I spoke to was extremely helpful.
gaps.explanation: 'Whom' is the formal object form after a preposition-style clause.

gaps.sentence: The author, about ___ there has been much debate, will speak at the festival.
gaps.hint: debate about the author — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: 'About whom' is required after the preposition 'about' when referring to a person.

gaps.sentence: The programme ___ I watched last night was about volcanoes.
gaps.explanation: 'Which' refers to things, even when it is the object of the clause.

gaps.sentence: The man ___ wallet I found works at the post office.
gaps.explanation: 'Whose wallet' means 'the man's wallet'; 'who's' means 'who is' and cannot precede a noun.

gaps.sentence: The village ___ my grandmother was born has no shops.
gaps.explanation: 'Where' is the relative adverb for places; 'which' cannot stand alone here because no preposition is present.
'What I meant' means 'the thing that I meant'; 'that I meant' would be an incomplete relative clause.

gaps.sentence: The manager, for ___ the team played so hard, thanked everyone.
gaps.hint: played for the manager — person after preposition
gaps.explanation: The preposition 'for' demands the object form 'whom' for a person.
